title: Is Moving Entire Game Code Between Different Agents a Bad Idea?
author: TRIPMINE_Guy
selftext:
I have a functioning rts godot game that has alot of working features (ai pathing, shooting, collision, some small physics, stage based destroyable buildings, unit building) but I have hit my grokbot cap in one night. I really want to continue and have contemplated getting the next tier at $100 but I have read people online saying the newer grok subscriptions (mine is legacy $30) have lower usage caps which makes me think that might be a bad idea.

I asked my bot early on to write a report of what we were doing in the event I ever migrated. Do you think getting a $20 claude subscription and feeding it that document and giving context will be horrible or counterproductive? I'm so far very impressed with what has been done so far in grokbot and don't want to create some problem in ability by passing the problem back and forth between claude and grok when the caps run out.

also my entire game code is only 25kb which seems nuts but it's using really bare bones graphics right now. I'm also 100% coding with english I have no coding experience that would be useful.

comments.author: Additional-Hippo5882
comments.body: You would be better off upgrading to a $100 tier than switching between accounts

comments.author: Wide-Bobcat-3723
comments.body: Wdym sharing back and forth? Just push your code to GitHub and have each agent work on their own branches then push your agreed changes to main. I have like 18 different agents working in my project lol

replies.author: TRIPMINE_Guy
replies.body: I guess I'm not very experienced with that like I said I'm just vibe coding with language the entire project. How does that work when one ai is doing massive overhaul to the physics or pathfinding of the game? For example if I am adding air units on one bot and messing with pathfinding optimizations on another, i feel like that would scew up because they both would touch pathfinding.

replies.author: Wide-Bobcat-3723
replies.body:
They see each other’s changes on github in real time and ask you how you want to resolve conflicts and one can bring another's code in or merge the changes onto the main branch.

Just watch a few YouTube videos on git.

replies.author: Gestaltarskiten
replies.body:
Ask a bot how to set it up in a shared workspace on you local machine (with git support). It will produce suggestions for claude.md, agents.md, maybe suggest a baton.md, et cetera - ask it how this is made efficient and without bloat and try these new routines.
But most important, keep studying and try to teach yourself so you understand what is happening and why.

replies.author: Itchy_Ship2584
replies.body:
i use codex/claude/gemini, each is better at specific things and they each handle their role in the 'team'

they can communicate via mcp when needed to coordinate and obviously in their own worktrees/branches with github

gemini neon = designs/plans the work packets

codex astra 5.2 = implements the packets

claude opus 5.5 = tests and validates the game in testing and sends visual screenshots/test results back to neon

comments.author: Arcodiant
comments.body: You should have all your work planned and tracked in documents anyway, that helps the agents stay organised; but also, mix and match agents for complementary tasks. Have one write the design and the other implement. Have one write code and the other review. Have one write tests and the other get them to pass, etc

comments.author: dtlater
comments.body: Have your agent write your design summary in a markdown file in the repo, or in an external doc they can all access, and new agents won't have to reanalyze everything from scratch

comments.author: StoneCypher
comments.body: It can be done but it takes effort.  That said, you can easily decompose your game into libraries, and have individual agents handle individual libraries.

comments.author: Toastti
comments.body:
The grok bot has already removed from its context large portions of the conversation from earlier. It's no big deal to move. They will keep going based on the agents.md content, the documentation in the repo, the comments in the code, the roadmap for the game etc.

So before you switch just make sure you have all of those. And you are completely fine to move over.

When you do switch ask your new agent to find the grok sessions on your computer and fully read through the one you developed your game on. It will do this and then understand what has been done so far and what is upcoming

Also I highly suggest getting the $100 Claude plan. It has same weekly usage as the $200 plan, you just have to split your work up more due to 5 hour linit

comments.author: Vegetable_Voice_2044
comments.body:
I moved my google gemini project over to the $20 claude pro subscription without any problems. 70 scripts, of which two of them were 1k+ lines. (i have many small scripts)

the claude usage rate is much better than what i was getting with google gemini when it came to generating, or updating the code.

after doing that i found out i could have just given claude the folder of my entire project to read them from there... coulda saved myself some time.

comments.author: DaedalusRaistlin
comments.body:
Here's the thing - to most agents, any new conversation will involve rereading your entire codebase to figure out how to do what you want. 

Handing it to a different AI agent is basically the same thing. There shouldn't be any noticeable difference. 

I was using GitHub Copilot in VS Code for a while, and was switching between different agents constantly. They all have their strengths and weaknesses, but they all have to review your code again at the start of every new conversation.

Personally I prefer Claude, after having tried quite a few different models. It just seems to understand the code better and make smarter decisions. Gemini was one of the worst, I find that's only good for initial prototypes - it made so many bad coding decisions, like sampling my JSON data then hardcoding a few lines of that data into my source code.

comments.author: Any-Blacksmith-2054
comments.body: You will never regret switch to $20 Claude. This is day and night comparing to grok

replies.author: TRIPMINE_Guy
replies.body:
yeah I have been reading claude is better. The thing is grokbot hasn't made any mistakes so far and my game so far seems really built out without any bugs yet.  I even asked it what type of optimizations rts usually makes and asked it to implement those. idk if it was actually effective though. I just found out i can just use grok directly attached to my game folder though. I was using grokbot because I thought the alternative was copy and pasting code into chat online and running the programs manually that it spits out which was very slow.

although grokbot apparently has been running hundreds of simulations of my game on its terminal for each change so maybe that's why it hasn't had bugs lol. it uploads pictures of it running my game.

replies.author: Any-Blacksmith-2054
replies.body:
I understand; but Claude will do everything that grok did, and so much better! You will see yourself. Don't hesitate and spend those $20, I did the same two weeks ago and still excited. What I get (I was only voice commanding Claude, didn't touch keyboard) https://maxims.top/

All games/sites/assets created by Claude in just 2 damn weeks

replies.author: Ok-Sea300
replies.body:
Not entirely true, anything story related should go to grok. Grok will let you kill enemies instead of neutralizing and "letting them go".

Code wise though, claude all the way

comments.author: YouKnowItsMeStudios
comments.body: I'll tell you right now, if you're on a low tier for Claude, that first migration prompt will eat about 35% or more of your 5 hour limit cause Claude needs to pull everything into context.

comments.author: dr0idattack137
comments.body: Ask Claude or agent of choice to setup git, GitHub , use Cyrus (for agent control) plus Linear (for backlog ) , scheduled cron jobs to check process is flowing. Start out your game with a PRD, built from an agent asking the what, why, when, how, where, who of your idea, and breaking it into todos / issues for your backlog. I know sounds less vibe codey but some process helps.
